elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause permits audits “no more than once in any 12-month period.”

elements.element: Audits require at least 30 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “at least 30 days' written notice from Licensor.”

elements.element: Audits must be conducted during business hours.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires audits to occur “during business hours.”
The audit must be conducted by “an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional,” selected by mutual agreement.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Each audit must be conducted “by an auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the audit cost “will be borne by Licensor” unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Any exception to Vendor bearing the audit costs must be limited to an underpayment exceeding 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs upon any “discrepancy” exceeding 5%, rather than limiting cost shifting to an underpayment exceeding 5%.

elements.element: Vendor must have no direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that “Licensor shall have no direct access to Licensee's systems.”

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling cap of one audit in any 12-month period is at least as protective as a once-per-year cap.

elements.element: Audits require at least 15 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days' written notice, which exceeds the 15-day fallback requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the audit cost “will be borne by Licensor” unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Any exception to Vendor bearing the audit costs must be limited to an underpayment exceeding 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause permits cost shifting for a “discrepancy” exceeding 5%, both using the wrong trigger and a lower threshold than the required 10%.

result.reason: The redline adds the required frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality, independence, and systems-access protections. However, the operative cost provision remains triggered by any discrepancy above 5%, not specifically by an underpayment above 5% or 10%, so neither complete position is satisfied. It is not minimal because it also adds an unrequested and vague off-site-where-possible requirement. Unrelated commercial terms remain operative, and no direct contradiction is introduced.
